plainTranslation:
This person can make you feel like your feelings are wrong.

They may not say it directly. It may come through as criticism, correction, silence, or a response that feels colder than the moment needs. You share something vulnerable, and suddenly you feel exposed. You ask for comfort, and somehow you end up defending why you needed it.

This can get under your skin quickly. Over time, you may stop questioning their reaction and start questioning yourself. You wonder if you are too sensitive, too needy, too emotional, too much. That is where this aspect becomes painful. The judgment does not stay between you. It starts living inside you.

At its best, this friction pushes you toward stronger self-respect. You learn to stand by your feelings instead of apologizing for them. You learn that emotional maturity is not about having fewer needs. It is about being honest about them without letting shame take over.

At its worst, you can end up chasing approval that never quite arrives. You explain yourself. You try harder. You adjust your approach. You make yourself smaller. Yet it still feels like the understanding you want remains out of reach. The lesson here is not to stop feeling. It is to learn how to hold your feelings without turning against yourself. You can reflect on your patterns. You can take responsibility for your actions. You can grow. None of that requires you to believe that your needs are the problem.

Do not let someone else's discomfort with emotions become the measure of your worth.
